name: Name
title: Reports
indexedNote: An indexed operator is answered by the directory without reading every person. A query on users whose filter uses none of them, or that sorts or counts, reads every person: it is refused when run synchronously and becomes a job when the mode is auto.
because.everyPerson: This query was queued as a job because its filter is not one the directory can answer from an index, so it has to read every person. A filter on username, mail or entryUuid is answered at once.
because.asked: This query was queued as a job because it asked to run as one.
because.limit: This query was queued as a job because its limit is above the synchronous cap.
because.source: This query was queued as a job because its source cannot be read synchronously.
because.run: This job is a saved definition run by hand.
because.schedule: This job is a scheduled run of a saved definition.
scheduleYearly: On {date} at {time} UTC, every year. Tick weekdays to repeat weekly instead.
groupsNote: The groups this definition is shared with. Their members can run it and read its result, and when a job of it finishes with Notify on, each group is emailed at its own address. A group with no address is written up as an error instead.
tipSource: The catalog source the report reads: one table of the catalog, such as users or auditEvents. A report names one source.
tipFields: The columns the result carries, in catalog order. Untick a field to leave it out. A count ignores this list and carries the group field and count.
tipFilter: Which rows are kept. Each row is a field, an operator and a value; several rows must all hold (and). Press + for another row. On a large directory a users filter on username, mail or entryUuid is answered from an index; any other filter reads every person and runs as a job.
tipSort: The field the rows are ordered by, and the direction. An ordered read has to see every matching row before it answers.
tipLimit: The most rows the result carries. Over the synchronous cap the query becomes a job.
tipFormat: JSON, CSV (RFC 4180) or PDF. A PDF has a row cap of its own; ask for CSV for more.
tipCount: Count the matching rows instead of listing them, one number per value of the group field.
tipGroupBy: The low-cardinality field a count is grouped by, such as status or protocol.
tipSaveQuery: Keep this query as a named definition you can run again, schedule and share. Ticked, the Name box and the Save button appear.
tipName: The name the definition is listed under.
tipRunAt: The time of day, in UTC, a scheduled run starts; the date is used when no weekday is ticked.
tipRepeatOn: The weekdays the schedule repeats on, at the time above. None ticked means the one date above, every year.
tipEnabled: Whether the schedule runs. Off, the definition keeps its schedule and runs only by hand.
tipNotify: Email the owner and every shared group when a job of this definition finishes. A shared group with no email address is written up as an error.
tipGroupSearch: Part of a group's name or DN. Five hits a page; Add puts a group on the list below.
tipParameters: A JSON object of values for the parameters the saved filter names, for this run only. Leave it empty to use the stored defaults.
tipTrustRealm: The trust realm this page is showing. Choosing another opens that realm's reports application, where you sign in again.
parametersHelp: A filter leaf may name a parameter instead of a value, such as {leaf}; the definition stores a default for it, and a run fills it from the box above, for example {example}. A key given here overrides the stored default for this run only.
parametersNone: This definition names no parameter, so the box is ignored.
accounts.summaryTitle: This tab is signed in as {user}. The other accounts signed in in this browser, and a sign-in as another account. Switching changes this tab only.
accounts.switchTitle: Use this tab as {user}. Other tabs keep the accounts they are.
accounts.none: No other account is signed in in this browser yet.
accounts.anotherTitle: Sign in as a different person in this tab. The accounts already signed in in this browser stay signed in, and other tabs keep theirs.
accounts.kept: The account this tab leaves stays signed in, so you can switch back to it here.
accounts.refused: The sign-in came back as another account than the one chosen, so this tab did not take it.
accounts.failed: The sign-in as the other account could not be started.
